title: Week 22 Mastery Quiz · International Organizations and Global Governance

questions.question: UN Charter Article 24 assigns primary international peace-and-security responsibility to which body?
options: The Secretariat acting alone.
The International Court of Justice in every political dispute.
The Security Council, subject to its Charter mandate and institutional constraints.
The General Assembly acting as an executive government.
questions.explanation: The Security Council, subject to its Charter mandate and institutional constraints.

questions.question: A simulated General Assembly important-question vote has 150 members present and voting; 98 favor it. Under Charter Article 18 what follows?
options: It passes because 98 exceeds half.
It passes automatically as a unanimous decision.
Its passage depends only on absent members.
It falls short of the two-thirds threshold of 100 votes.
questions.explanation: It falls short of the two-thirds threshold of 100 votes.

questions.question: A briefing treats a General Assembly recommendation as legally identical to a Security Council decision. What must be corrected?
options: The bodies' Charter powers and legal consequences must be distinguished.
Both documents are automatically enforceable treaties.
General Assembly votes always bind all courts.
Institutional identity cannot affect legal force.
questions.explanation: The bodies' Charter powers and legal consequences must be distinguished.

questions.question: A regional organization publishes a public health coordination plan. What additional evidence measures actual implementation?
options: The organization's formal name alone.
Funding, member participation, operational delivery and independently measured results.
The number of languages on its website.
Its date of founding without activity data.
questions.explanation: Funding, member participation, operational delivery and independently measured results.

questions.question: A fictional council adopts a resolution, but two parties interpret its timetable differently. What should an implementation review do?
options: Select whichever press release is longer.
Assume disagreement proves deliberate bad faith.
Examine the adopted text, competent interpretations, dates and verified compliance records.
Substitute a previous unrelated resolution.
questions.explanation: Examine the adopted text, competent interpretations, dates and verified compliance records.

questions.question: An analysis claims the WTO and WHO perform interchangeable tasks because both are international organizations. What improves the comparison?
options: Compare only staff counts.
Assume all organizations issue equivalent binding orders.
Use one agency's budget as the other's authority.
Examine founding mandates, membership, decision mechanisms and policy domains separately.
questions.explanation: Examine founding mandates, membership, decision mechanisms and policy domains separately.

questions.question: A statistical brief compares contributions from states of different sizes. Which denominator matters when drawing an equity claim?
options: Select and justify a measure such as share of national income, alongside absolute contributions.
Use raw totals as automatically fair.
Exclude countries with different currencies.
Assume national population alone determines payment obligations.
questions.explanation: Select and justify a measure such as share of national income, alongside absolute contributions.

questions.question: A fictional regional peacekeeping mission announces success based only on deployed personnel. What outcome evidence is missing?
options: The troop count repeated twice.
Mandate fulfillment, civilian protection indicators, access and unintended harms.
The mission flag's design.
A list of official ceremonies.
questions.explanation: Mandate fulfillment, civilian protection indicators, access and unintended harms.

questions.question: UN Charter Article 25 concerns carrying out Security Council decisions. Which caution is appropriate?
options: Article 25 converts all Assembly debates into decisions.
Only national constitutions determine whether a Council decision exists.
Interpret the specific decision and Charter context rather than assuming every Council statement has identical effect.
Every Council document is a new treaty.
questions.explanation: Interpret the specific decision and Charter context rather than assuming every Council statement has identical effect.

questions.question: A governance report uses one member state's statement as proof of unanimous institutional policy. What should be checked?
options: The member state's press office logo.
The length of the statement.
How many journalists reposted it.
Adopted decisions and voting or consensus records, distinguishing member positions from organization acts.
questions.explanation: Adopted decisions and voting or consensus records, distinguishing member positions from organization acts.

shortResponse: When can international organizations solve collective problems, and when do power, design, or sovereignty limit them?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
